newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada imposes duties on steel plate imports.
newsitem.headline: Canada imposes duties on steel plate imports.

text.p: The Canadian government said on Friday it will impose provisional anti-dumping duties on hot-rolled carbon steel plate imported from Mexico, China, South Africa and Russia.
Revenue Canada said it launched an investigation into steel plate imports in February after Stelco Inc complained that the dumping of low-priced steel plate was harming the Canadian industry.
The government department said it is no longer investigating imports of steel plate from Poland because of the low volumes involved.
But it said preliminary results from its investigation showed prices are on average 24.3 percent below fair levels.
Canada said China's prices were 23.9 percent below fair levels, Mexico's prices were 26.2 percent too low, South Africa was off 18.1 percent and Russia's discount was 25.3 percent.
The Canadian market consumed hot-rolled steel plate worth about C$500 million in 1996. About 80 percent of that amount was produced in Canada.

The Canadian International Trade Tribunal will conduct a full inquiry into whether dumping is hurting the Canadian production of hot-rolled steel plate and will hold public hearings, the government statement said. The tribunal is to make its decision by Oct. 27.
Revenue Canada said it plans to continue its own investigation and make a final decision on dumping by Sept. 25.
Earlier this month, the secretariat for the North American Free Trade Agreement told Mexico that its anti-dumping duties aimd at Canadian steel exporters were flawed.
